reason: Arm structure (true tensor vs dense vs low-rank surrogate, same affine part, same Boolean field eqs) is a valid null/control layout and the metric (closure degree d_F, dim W_d) is structural, not wall time. Four defects as written. (1) Regime overlap: d_F(arm A) is about 3-4 at n<=17 (treatise certifies >=5 only at n=33-45), and a random Boolean quadratic system with ~N equations in N=2k=12-18 variables has semi-regular/refutation degree about 4-5 at these sizes, so the claimed 'arm B >=6 at n=13' is not expected; the k+2 bound (8-11) exceeds the cap 6, so 'tracks k+2' is undetectable. All arms likely land in {3,4,5} and prediction_if_true is indistinguishable from prediction_if_false branch 'arm B also low'. (2) Cost: closure to degree 6 on N=18 has 31,180 columns and ~4k multipliers x n polys (~60k rows) per iteration; GF(2) elimination in numpy is ~1e11-1e12 word ops per closure, times 96 closures plus iteration to stability: well over 20 CPU-min in python. Degree <=4 is cheap. (3) Arm C (random F_2-rank-n) is the wrong surrogate: mu_V has K-bar rank n with Galois-conjugate rank-ones, F_2-rank >= 2n-1 (Chudnovsky/Shokrollahi), so random F_2 rank n is not a model of mu_V (already flagged in MP-comm_alg-1.refute.json). Arm D ranks {2n,3n} are F_2-ranks and do not interpolate toward mu_V either. (4) Unsat-target requirement: 2k vs n equations gives ~2^(2k-n) expected solutions (about 2 at k=ceil(n/2)), so unsat draws need rejection sampling, with biased selection differing across arms; and extrapolation n=11-17 -> 131 is a slope claim from 4 points with censoring, weak. No decision rule is given for 'within one degree on >=80%' vs noise at 6 draws. Toy-only artefact unless converted to a growth-in-n structural quantity.
